title: Minimax Testing of Constant CATE over a Bounded Holder Class with Rough Confounding
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < 7.2; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The note proves the advertised full-class bracket and a matched oracle-rate result only in the no-penalty region; throughout the strict rough-confounding regime it supplies an upper rate but no nuisance-scale converse, so it does not establish the complete minimax frontier suggested by the title.

The claim that the attaining test is explicitly computable is under-documented because the projectors, basis normalization, grid-rounding rules, and numerical constructions of C_B and C_0 are described generically rather than specified sufficiently for direct independent implementation.

The missing rough-regime characterization, impractical worst-case arithmetic cost, and absence of computational evidence for the proposed calibration keep the projected paper below the matched-frontier calibration anchors.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a same-class two-sided observational minimax bracket, constructed a total higher-order corrected-energy test for its upper endpoint, and matched the oracle rate throughout the no-penalty region, including the equality boundary without a logarithmic loss. The attempted correlated propensity–baseline lower-bound mixture did not control all observed transition regions and could transfer impermissible CATE roughness into the baseline when beta exceeds gamma. A field-level revival therefore needs a new legal composite-null mixture establishing the strict rough-regime converse, together with fully executable projector/calibration constants and computational evidence.
tldr: For constant-CATE testing over the exact observed-data image of the bounded causal Hölder class, the strongest proved result is the full-class bracket \(c_{\mathrm{rate}}r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\le\rho_\star(n)\le C_{\mathrm{rate}}\{r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\vee r_{\mathrm{nu}}(n)\}\). The endpoints coincide exactly when \(\alpha+\beta\ge2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), including equality without a logarithmic loss, so rough confounding has no minimax-rate penalty throughout that region. The upper endpoint is attained by an explicit, terminating, uniformly calibrated higher-order corrected-energy test with deterministic tuning. Only the strict complementary regime remains open: whether \(r_{\mathrm{nu}}\) is sharp, whether \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) create separate elbows, and whether further rough-regime boundaries carry logarithms. Yu (2026) and Dhawan--Guo--Shah (2026) are procedure-level power comparators under additional learner, direction, variance, and regularity conditions, not uniform full-class minimax comparators.
gap: Existing observational homogeneity tests document asymptotic size and power under learned-direction, learner-remainder, or multisample U-statistic conditions; existing Hölder theory treats CATE estimation, direct regression, conditional-mean independence under different classes, or heteroskedasticity rather than the declared constant-CATE experiment.
fill: The project targets an algorithmic upper bound and matching observational converse on one unchanged statistical class through an exact full-law-to-observed-image bridge, a profiled bounded-weight score, deterministic local-polynomial product correction, independent higher-order cross-energy, and a null-preserving observed-likelihood mixture program; the risk-projection lemma places Yu and Dhawan--Guo--Shah on the phase map under their own conditions.
